## Facts

### P257 plan: drop git line add/remove counts

- km_pzyngdg3b9se P257 removes per-file and per-directory added/removed line counts from the git UI and stops the git --numstat spawns used only for those counts. Per-file status indicators (kind letter, rename original path, similarity) are kept and come from --name-status.
- km_46dbcdjcmhxf Line counts render in packages/git-ui FileTree.vue (directory and file rows, tree and flat modes) and in the ADE Changes tab (AdeChangesTab.vue fileDelta). No per-commit count exists.
- km_cmf5ew694hrg The isBinary flag is dropped from FileChange (Go, git-ipc, git-core) and binary from the ADE wire, with no replacement. No list consumer remains, and the diff view detects binary per file at diff time.
- km_7erm0446znby Rejected for the binary flag: a numstat spawn kept only for binary (costs a full content diff for an unused flag), git diff --raw (gives modes and oids, not binaryness), and check-attr (sees only attributes, not content).
- km_521pd5cx67xr Stash list (StashListArgs) and global stash log (GlobalStashLogArgs) keep --numstat though counts are not displayed, because its record shape lets collectNumstatRecs tell a header from a path record by position (e.g. a file named stash@{0} or a 40-hex name).
- km_f3vzbk0y5v87 ParseNumstatRecords and fillCounts stay. NumstatEntry shrinks to Path and OriginalPath; counts are still validated as '-' or int but not stored.
- km_zy7w3zmx4060 PreflightStashPop in gitsession/preflight.go needs only paths, so it switches from numstat to --name-status. Stash paths come from fileChanges(ctx, NameStatusArgs(...)) using Path only, for parity with numstat's new-path-only list.
- km_fc3abhpwskks Numstat spawns are dropped in gitsession fileChanges (CommitDetail), StashShow, WorkingDetail, RangeFiles (incremental.go) and queuefacts.go (ADE branch files).
- km_v0sc64rh57bn fileChanges(ctx, args) returns []porcelain.FileChange via runRecords plus ParseNameStatusRecords, without an errgroup. StashShowArgs and WorkingNumstatArgs are deleted; stash callers use NameStatusArgs(&base, sha).
- km_6fm7a4ps0a08 ParseNameStatusRecords now returns []FileChange directly (OriginalPath set when non-empty; Similarity set for renamed/copied). Go porcelain FileChange loses Additions, Deletions, IsBinary.
- km_f382wtjw55ps NumstatArgs, CombineFileChanges and NameStatusEntry are deleted because there is nothing to merge with one input.
- km_kgcx23szzfp0 A name-status row with no matching numstat row used to be silently dropped and now shows. A git 2.43 probe found no such case in real output.
- km_ndy2pfa9m3q9 The FileTree directory row keeps the 'N file(s)' text and drops only the +x -y aggregate, since a file count is not a line count. fileTreeModel.ts drops additions/deletions from directory nodes and the aggregation but keeps fileCount.

### P257 plan: drop git line add/remove counts > 3. Work

- km_vnth10dngx0w The TS git-ipc and git-core FileChange types drop additions, deletions and isBinary.
- km_g86xxh5vef02 git-ui FileTree.vue removes the count display but keeps 'N files', status letter, rename display and tips. countFormat.ts and its test are deleted as sole-consumer code.

### P257 plan: drop git line add/remove counts

- km_be2g2h202ekn The ADE Changes tab drops its delta column and shows a plain truncating path per file row (conflict tint unchanged), because keeping counts would need a numstat spawn for ADE alone.
- km_vg8f9773ykp5 ADE wire FileChange keeps only Path (loses Added, Deleted, Binary). The wire has no version (P143 freeze rule), so Go adewire and TS ade/v2/wire.ts must change together.
- km_q5tx1yvn9n3a Removing git contract fields is breaking, so ContractVersion goes 47 -> 48 in Go gitrpc/contract.go (with a 'P257: 47 -> 48, breaking.' comment), TS git-ipc validate.ts CONTRACT_VERSION, tests pinning 47, and the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md version line (48, P257).

stored.fact: internal/llmprompts holds every LLM prompt and LLM-facing instruction both apps send. It is not internal/prompts (the P246 popup router).
registry.go is the only file containing prompt text. Each entry has id, kind, apps, title/purpose/usedBy catalog keys, applies-when, default, required fragments and fixed output schema.
Registry entries use typed handle Prompt[V] with Text(src, vars). Entries without variables use NoVars.
The prompt registry has 85 entries: Space lists 61, Studio lists 33.
User-authored text (smart-script bodies, workflow stage and step prompts) stays out of the prompt registry.
Prompt kinds are system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument (one MCP tool property description, with Parent tool and Field), toolResult, and fragment (included via {{template}}).
InputSchema[T] sets each tool property's description from its argument entry; a mismatch panics at server build. jsonschema struct tags are not used.
Prompts use text/template, one set per resolve, with only the funcs inc and join. An entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
Default prompts render byte-identical to the pre-P271 output (testdata/golden).
RenderParts wraps each string variable in marker runes and splits, so Settings Preview marks resolved values with VarText. A failed self-check returns one literal part.

Prompt overrides are stored per app in <home>/llm-prompts.json (~/.kira-studio/, ~/.kira-space/), written with renameio, mode 0600, shape {version, revision, overrides: {id: {text, defaultHash, updatedAt}}}.
Saving the default text removes the prompt override.
Override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash; a stale change is refused with E_CONFLICT.

If the store file is corrupt or an override no longer validates, the default is used, a warning is logged, and Settings flags it (storeError, invalid). defaultChanged flags an override made against an older default.
Server-side validation requires the template to parse, every prompt:"required" variable to be referenced, every required fragment to be included, and execution against example vars to succeed.
Memory system prompts must include the memory.dataHygiene fragment, because it is the injection defence.
Schema-bound prompts (gate, reconcile, import extract and finalize) keep their JSON schema fixed; it shows read-only in Settings.

There is no global prompt source. Consumers receive a llmprompts.Source (Resolve, Revision) through their options (memory.ServiceOptions, mcpserver.Options, claudeheadless, scriptruns, ADE, dbmcp). Defaults() is the registry-only source.
Store.Resolve stats the file per call and re-reads it on mtime or size change.
Gate, reconcile, import, headless suffixes and ADE messages resolve prompts per call, so an edit applies on the next call.
memory-mcp (a stdio subprocess) builds server instructions and tool and argument descriptions once per process, so prompt edits apply only to new Claude sessions (newSession, shown in Settings).
dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild their MCP server when Revision() changes.
Both apps expose LlmPromptsService (List, Save, Preview) and emit event kira:llmPrompts:changed with {revision}.
LlmPromptsService Save is all-or-nothing, with per-id errors returned as an E_BAD_REQUEST payload.
Preview with real vars also renders the ADE run dialog and step inspector, so no TS copy of a prompt exists.
The Settings section Prompts sits before Advanced in both apps (packages/workbench/src/llmPrompts/) with list, Monaco editor, Changes diff against default, Preview and per-entry reset.
Prompt drafts live in Pinia store llmPromptDrafts; the Settings dialog Save saves prompts first, then the settings patch.

The guard go run ./internal/llmprompts/cmd/checkprompts (part of bun run lint) fails on a jsonschema tag, an mcp Tool/Prompt/PromptArgument Description or ServerOptions Instructions not from llmprompts, or a memory.Call System not from llmprompts.

The checkprompts guard also fails on a copy of a registry default (first 48 characters; whole text when 24 to 47) in a non-test .go, .ts or .vue file outside internal/llmprompts and internal/flowtest.

stored.fact: An agent-started import job may run at most 300 chunks (autoStartChunks) without the user's consent.
Run returns ErrRunnerBusy when another runner holds the store's lock; this is a supported state.
Only the Agent option is required in RunnerOptions.
The Runner schedules bulk imports (scan, materialise, extract, finalize); exactly one runs per memory.db, held by an exclusive flock.
The Runner polls the job rows written by the control side (Engine), so a pause or cancel from another process takes effect within one tick.
All Runner state lives in memory.db, so a halted runner resumes from disk.
NewRunner takes no lock; the lock is taken only in Run, which works until ctx ends or the store has been idle for IdleExit.
A runner taking the lock resets what a crashed predecessor left mid-flight (running jobs become paused, scanning jobs rescan) and never resumes a job by itself.

tryExit releases the lock, then checks once more for work a control call wrote meanwhile, because a job set running just before the release would otherwise find no runner; if work exists it takes the lock again.
On shutdown with recover, running jobs end paused as interrupted and in-flight chunks go back to pending; an idle exit has nothing to recover.
Pause, cancel and finish disarm a job's context, which kills its in-flight calls.
sync reads job states from the control side: running jobs get a context, jobs that left running lose theirs, scanning jobs get a scan, and finished jobs settle.
